cache-stampede:cdn:launch.title: A hot item's expiry would flood Product API.
cache-stampede:cdn:launch.message: Launch page's most popular item gets 320/s. Each time it expires, about 61 requests reach Product API before the first reply. Cold cache probe: hard purge at 5 s, replay to 20 s at configured rates.
cache-stampede:cdn:launch.rationale: Cache benefits depend on item reuse. Cold-cache probes use configured traffic, not saved story peaks; replay budgets can leave caches unchecked.
cache-stampede:cdn:launch.shownMessage: ⁨Launch page⁩'s most popular item gets 320/s. Each time it expires, about 61 requests reach ⁨Product API⁩ before the first reply. Cold cache probe: hard purge at 5 s, replay to 20 s at configured rates. Readers may receive old data while it refreshes. Choose this only where that loss of freshness is acceptable.
cache-stampede:cdn:launch.shownRationale: Cache benefits depend on item reuse. Probes use configured traffic, not saved story peaks; replay budgets can leave caches unchecked.

cache-cold-start:cdn:launch.title: Product API can't carry Edge CDN's traffic when the cache is cold.
cache-cold-start:cdn:launch.message: After a purge or deploy, Product API gets 400/s, 8.0× its capacity, until the cache refills. Cold cache probe: hard purge at 5 s, replay to 20 s; no recovery within 10 s.
cache-cold-start:cdn:launch.rationale: Cache benefits depend on item reuse. Cold-cache probes use configured traffic, not saved story peaks; replay budgets can leave caches unchecked.
cache-cold-start:cdn:launch.shownMessage: After a purge or deploy, ⁨Product API⁩ gets 400/s, 8× its capacity, until the cache refills. The probe did not recover within 10 s. Cold cache probe: hard purge at 5 s, replay to 20 s at configured rates.
cache-cold-start:cdn:launch.shownRationale: Cache benefits depend on item reuse. Probes use configured traffic, not saved story peaks; replay budgets can leave caches unchecked.

single-point:origin.title: Every request goes through one Product API
single-point:origin.message: It runs 1 replica, and every request from Shoppers goes through it: if it stops, Shoppers gets nothing.
single-point:origin.rationale: Redundancy is what turns one instance's availability into a service's: with two replicas, one can stop (a deploy, a crash, a node drained) while the other answers.
